## Director

### Joseph Bulbulia

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%"}
![Joseph Bulbulia](images/team/joseph-bulbulia.jpg){.team-photo}
:::

::: {.column width="75%"}
**Director, OTTO Lab**  
[joseph.bulbulia@vuw.ac.nz](mailto:joseph.bulbulia@vuw.ac.nz) · [University Profile](https://people.wgtn.ac.nz/joseph.bulbulia) · [Full CV](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/jtlekxwxf05rfu1dw5hw9/bulbulia-j-a-cv.pdf?rlkey=4mink1sq6hftvje39t4y53s46&dl=0)

**About**

OTTO Lab is based in the [School of Psychological Sciences](https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/psyc) at Te Herenga Waka — Victoria University of Wellington.

Joseph Bulbulia teaches and researches in the [School of Psychological Sciences](https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/psyc) at Victoria University of Wellington. His research investigates the causes of human cooperation, conflict, and well-being, with a focus on the role of religion and values. Joseph specialises in methods for causal inference from observational data. He also directs the [Centre for Applied Cross-Cultural Research (CACR)](https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/cacr).

**Research Projects**
Joseph contributes to two major research projects:

1. **New Zealand Attitudes and Values Study (NZAVS)**: Joseph serves as a principal investigator on major NZAVS projects. He uses 15 years of repeated-measures longitudinal data from more than 76,000 New Zealanders to investigate religion, social cohesion, and trust.

2. **Pulotu Database of Pacific Religions**: As a founding co-investigator, Joseph uses this database of 116 Austronesian cultures to evaluate theories about the evolution of religious beliefs and their effects on social behaviour.

#### Supervision

Joseph supervises students in a broad range of areas, including:

- Personality and individual differences
- Political psychology
- Well-being and flourishing
- Religion (his primary interest)
:::

## The Ottos

### Otto Lilienthal

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%"}
![Otto Lilienthal](images/ottos/web/otto-lilienthal-portrait.jpg){.team-photo fig-alt="Otto Lilienthal in flight beneath a glider, above a sandy hillside, in 1891."}
:::

::: {.column width="75%"}
**Honorary Fellow, Direct Experimentation**

Otto (1848–1896) measured the flight of storks before he left the ground, and published the measurements in 1889. He then made more than two thousand glider flights between 1891 and 1896. The lab follows the first half of his method. Otto is not currently accepting students.

- **Project:** *Der Vogelflug als Grundlage der Fliegekunst* (1889)
- **Methods:** Observation, followed by experiment
- **Photograph:** Carl Kassner, 1891 (public domain)
:::

::::

### Otto (dog)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%"}
![Otto the dog](images/ottos/web/otto-dog-portrait.jpg){.team-photo fig-alt="A golden-brown dog looks over the back seat of a car."}
:::

::: {.column width="75%"}
**Research Fellow, Outcome Ascertainment**

Otto investigates the effect of a thrown ball on altitude. He serves as the study's only participant, and his adherence to treatment is complete. He joins the lab from Britain.

- **Project:** The ball
- **Methods:** Repeated measures
:::

::::

### Otto (cat)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%"}
![Otto the cat](images/ottos/web/otto-cat-portrait.jpg){.team-photo fig-alt="A tabby and white cat lies stretched out asleep on a sunlit wooden deck."}
:::

::: {.column width="75%"}
**Senior Fellow Emeritus, Control Condition**

Otto (2000–2015) served in the control arm for fifteen years, in New Zealand. He received no treatment and reported no complaints. Otto declined co-authorship on every paper, in advance.

- **Project:** None
- **Methods:** Remained at baseline
:::

::::

[New members of the lab are not required to be called Otto, although it would avoid confusion.]{.otto-note}
